title: Brown rice vs. quinoa: protein, fiber, and calories

seo.title: Brown rice vs. quinoa: protein, fiber, calories
seo.meta_description: Cooked quinoa and brown rice are both about 120 calories per 100 g. Quinoa provides more protein and fiber; brown rice provides somewhat more carbohydrate.
seo.search_intent: Compare cooked brown rice and quinoa for protein, fiber, carbohydrate, calories and micronutrients using the same food state.

excerpt: The calorie gap between cooked quinoa and brown rice is tiny: both are around 120 calories per 100 grams. Quinoa provides roughly 4.4 grams protein and 2.8 grams fiber versus about 2.7 grams and 1.6 grams in brown rice.
content_html:
Quinoa and brown rice are often treated as competitors, yet their cooked calorie density is almost identical; the clearer differences are protein, fiber, and selected micronutrients.

Per 100 g cooked

NutrientQuinoaBrown rice
Calories~120~123
Protein~4.4 g~2.7 g
Fiber~2.8 g~1.6 g
Carbohydrate~21.3 g~25.6 g
Fat~1.9 g~1.0 g

Quinoa provides about 1.7 g more protein and 1.2 g more fiber per 100 g, while brown rice provides roughly 4.3 g more carbohydrate. The calorie difference is only about 3 calories.

Cup servings make the protein gap more visible

One cup cooked quinoa, around 185 g, provides roughly 222 calories, 8.1 g protein, and 5.2 g fiber. A cup of cooked brown rice, around 195 g, is about 240 calories, 5.3 g protein, and 3.1 g fiber.

At those serving sizes, quinoa provides roughly 2.8 g more protein and 2.1 g more fiber.

Quinoa is not a high-protein food in the same sense as beans

Its 4.4 g protein/100 g beats rice, but cooked lentils provide about 9 g/100 g and firm tofu often 15–18 g/100 g. Quinoa’s advantage is meaningful among starch-rich staple foods, not equivalent to a main protein food.

Quinoa has a balanced amino-acid pattern

Quinoa contains all nine essential amino acids and is relatively rich in lysine compared with many grains. Total quantity still matters: 200 g cooked quinoa provides less than 9 g total protein.

Brown rice keeps the bran layer

Compared with white rice, brown rice retains outer grain layers and therefore provides more fiber, magnesium, and other nutrients. Quinoa having more fiber does not make brown rice fiber-free.

Compare cooked with cooked

Both foods absorb substantial water during cooking. Comparing dry quinoa with cooked rice creates misleading per-100-g numbers simply because the dry food contains far less water.

The useful takeaway

Cooked quinoa and brown rice are essentially tied in calories per 100 g. Quinoa provides more protein and fiber and has a strong amino-acid profile; brown rice contains somewhat more carbohydrate and remains a useful whole-grain staple. Texture, cost, and the rest of the meal can decide between them.

faq.question: Which has more protein, quinoa or brown rice?
faq.answer: Cooked quinoa: about 4.4 g/100 g versus roughly 2.7 g/100 g in cooked brown rice.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Quinoa in these references, at about 2.8 g/100 g versus 1.6 g/100 g.

faq.question: Which has fewer calories?
faq.answer: They are nearly tied: around 120 calories/100 g for quinoa and 123 for brown rice.
